texts.orig: Eye Health: Why You Should Schedule Your Annual Diabetes Eye Exam
texts.text: Eye Health: Why You Should Schedule Your Annual Diabetes Eye Exam

texts.label: text
texts.orig: As a person with diabetes, your annual eye exam is the best way to determine if your blood glucose (blood sugar) levels are affecting the health of your eyes. Even if your vision is completely normal and your eyes feel fine, you could be experiencing the earlier stages of a diabetes-related eye condition.
texts.text: As a person with diabetes, your annual eye exam is the best way to determine if your blood glucose (blood sugar) levels are affecting the health of your eyes. Even if your vision is completely normal and your eyes feel fine, you could be experiencing the earlier stages of a diabetes-related eye condition.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The sooner you catch diabetes-related eye conditions, the sooner they can be treated to prevent them from getting worse.
texts.text: The sooner you catch diabetes-related eye conditions, the sooner they can be treated to prevent them from getting worse.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your annual eye exam is one of the best ways to protect your eyes and help prevent future vision loss or blindness.
texts.text: Your annual eye exam is one of the best ways to protect your eyes and help prevent future vision loss or blindness.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Catching Diabetes Eye Complications Sooner Rather than Later
texts.text: Catching Diabetes Eye Complications Sooner Rather than Later

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your annual eye exam will look for signs of these five conditions, all of which can be largely prevented or minimized through managing healthy blood glucose (blood sugar) levels and consistently maintaining an A1C of less than 7 percent .
texts.text: Your annual eye exam will look for signs of these five conditions, all of which can be largely prevented or minimized through managing healthy blood glucose (blood sugar) levels and consistently maintaining an A1C of less than 7 percent .

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Retinopathy: Leakage, bleeding, and abnormal growth in the blood vessels of your eye's retina that can cause blindness
texts.text:  Retinopathy: Leakage, bleeding, and abnormal growth in the blood vessels of your eye's retina that can cause blindness

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Macular edema: Swelling and fluid build-up in the macula of your eye, the central part of the lightsensitive retina, often coincides with retinopathy and can cause severe vision loss.
texts.text:  Macular edema: Swelling and fluid build-up in the macula of your eye, the central part of the lightsensitive retina, often coincides with retinopathy and can cause severe vision loss.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Cataracts: Cloudiness in the lens of your eye that can cause vision loss
texts.text:  Cataracts: Cloudiness in the lens of your eye that can cause vision loss

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Glaucoma: Increased fluid pressure in your eyes that can damage the optic nerve, resulting in blindness if left untreated
texts.text:  Glaucoma: Increased fluid pressure in your eyes that can damage the optic nerve, resulting in blindness if left untreated

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Dry eye: People with diabetes are twice as likely to develop dry eye, which typically causes blurred vision that improves with blinking, excessive watering to compensate for the dryness, and severe stinging and burning of your eyes. Elevated blood glucose levels increase the risk of infection in patients with dry eye disease, which can result from a number of causes, including high blood glucose and a number of common prescription medicines.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: You should contact your optometrist immediately if you're experiencing any of the following:
texts.text: You should contact your optometrist immediately if you're experiencing any of the following:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Sudden difficulty reading or focusing on things close-up
texts.text:  Sudden difficulty reading or focusing on things close-up

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Sudden blurriness or double vision
texts.text:  Sudden blurriness or double vision

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Pressure or pain in your eyes
texts.text:  Pressure or pain in your eyes

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Presence of flashing lights, dark spots, or missing pieces in your vision
texts.text:  Presence of flashing lights, dark spots, or missing pieces in your vision

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Sudden appearance of floaters (moving spots or lines), especially when these are numerous
texts.text:  Sudden appearance of floaters (moving spots or lines), especially when these are numerous

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Appearance of red streaks in your vision
texts.text:  Appearance of red streaks in your vision

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Sudden worsening of your night vision
texts.text:  Sudden worsening of your night vision

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The most important thing to remember is that diabetes-related eye disease typically causes few or no symptoms until it is severe, so you should receive regular, dilated eye exams even when you are totally asymptomatic (no symptoms).
texts.text: The most important thing to remember is that diabetes-related eye disease typically causes few or no symptoms until it is severe, so you should receive regular, dilated eye exams even when you are totally asymptomatic (no symptoms).

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Your Annual Diabetes Eye Exam Includes These Four Tests:
texts.text: Your Annual Diabetes Eye Exam Includes These Four Tests:

texts.label: text
texts.orig: There are four parts of your routine diabetes eye exam. These tests are not painful.
texts.text: There are four parts of your routine diabetes eye exam. These tests are not painful.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Visual acuity testing: Using an eye chart to help determine your overall vision and whether you need glasses/contacts or an update to your current prescription.
texts.text:  Visual acuity testing: Using an eye chart to help determine your overall vision and whether you need glasses/contacts or an update to your current prescription.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Tonometry: Measures the pressure in your eye. High pressure could mean you're at risk for glaucoma, of which there are several types.
texts.text:  Tonometry: Measures the pressure in your eye. High pressure could mean you're at risk for glaucoma, of which there are several types.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Retinal imaging: Use of an imaging device that allows the eye doctor to detect very subtle changes to the health of your eyes.
texts.text:  Retinal imaging: Use of an imaging device that allows the eye doctor to detect very subtle changes to the health of your eyes.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig:  Dilated eye exam: After applying eye drops that enlarge your pupils, your eye doctor will be able to look into the back of your eye to detect any swelling of the retina, leaking blood vessels, nerve damage, cataracts, and other eye diseases that are more common in people with diabetes. This is the most important test for people with diabetes.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: How Often do I Need an Eye Exam?
texts.text: How Often do I Need an Eye Exam?

texts.label: text
texts.orig: For most people with diabetes, there is a very clear relationship between blood glucose (blood sugar) management, A1C results, and, more recently, glucose time-in-range and eye health. The more your blood glucose is in a safe range over time, you are less likely to develop any diabetes-related eye conditions.

The more your blood glucose is in a safe range over time, you are less likely to develop any diabetes-related eye conditions.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Type 1 diabetes: You need to have a dilated eye exam within five years of being diagnosed and every year after that.
texts.text: Type 1 diabetes: You need to have a dilated eye exam within five years of being diagnosed and every year after that.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Your first exam should include a dilated eye exam. Depending on the results, your doctor may approve waiting one to two years before you need another. If you are diagnosed with eye disease, the eye doctor may recommend seeing you more frequently.
texts.text: Your first exam should include a dilated eye exam. Depending on the results, your doctor may approve waiting one to two years before you need another. If you are diagnosed with eye disease, the eye doctor may recommend seeing you more frequently.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Type 2 diabetes: You need to have a dilated exam soon after your diabetes diagnosis. For many with type 2 diabetes, you could have been living with the disease for several years before your diagnosis, which means your eyes were at risk for damage without you or your physician even knowing it.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pregnancy with diabetes: If you are planning to get pregnant, have a complete eye exam prior to pregnancy. Once you learn you are pregnant, you'll want to have your eyes examined within the first trimester of your pregnancy, and again in the last trimester of your pregnancy to be sure that the increased stress from pregnancy hasn't affected your eye health.
texts.text: Pregnancy with diabetes: If you are planning to get pregnant, have a complete eye exam prior to pregnancy. Once you learn you are pregnant, you'll want to have your eyes examined within the first trimester of your pregnancy, and again in the last trimester of your pregnancy to be sure that the increased stress from pregnancy hasn't affected your eye health.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Pregnancy can increase the pressure on blood vessels throughout your eyes, increasing your risk of diabetes-related eye conditions, especially if you had signs of eye damage prior to getting pregnant.
texts.text: Pregnancy can increase the pressure on blood vessels throughout your eyes, increasing your risk of diabetes-related eye conditions, especially if you had signs of eye damage prior to getting pregnant.
